newsitem.title: FRANCE: Airbus head to meet EU panel on Boeing merger.
newsitem.headline: Airbus head to meet EU panel on Boeing merger.

text.p: The managing director of Airbus Industrie will present on Friday the aircraft consortium's concerns over a planned merger between Boeing and McDonnell Douglas to the European Commission, an Airbus spokesman said on Thursday.
Jean Pierson and financial controller Ian Massey will "provide evidence to the Commission's mergers task force" on Friday morning, the spokesman said.
The link-up between Boeing -McDonnell Douglas "has long-term implications which are detrimental to competition," he said.

Airbus strongly opposes the merger plan, which will create a $48 billion colossus in defence and civilian markets, dwarfing Airbus which had sales last year of $8.8 billion, down from $9.6 billion in 1995.

The four-nation consortium is particularly angered by the exclusive supplier agreements signed by Boeing with U.S. airlines. Continental on Tuesday joined AMR's American Airlines and Delta Air Lines in agreeing to buy all its planes from Boeing.
Airbus fears it is systematically being locked out of the vast U.S. airline market by these sole-supplier deals.
The Commission has until July 31 to make a ruling on the $14 billion merger plan.

Boeing has historically held around 60 percent of the world civilian aircraft market, Airbus around 30 percent, with McDonnell Douglas accounting for the rest. McDonnell Douglas has a strong defence operation.
European aerospace executives say the significant state funding for defence research which McDonnell Dougals receives will support the civilian sector in the merged company.
